title: Demigod review (2009)
partialText: One of the gods has fallen. Demigod is your chance to replace him. The problem? The other seven applicants.

title: Debate: What truly is the easiest character to cosplay?
partialText: Sometimes the prep and planning just doesn't cut it.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth's director weighs in on the real-time versus turn-based debate, saying that younger players 'increasingly favour more real-time experiences in games'
partialText: But Hamaguchi still reckons that turn-based games are "deeply universal."

title: Star Citizen's latest alpha update brings a 'full reset' to its universe, as Cloud Imperium Games promises to crack down on player exploits and duplication issues
partialText: Players keep their blueprints and ships bought with in-game currency, but that's it.

title: Civilization 7's imminent update will add one of history's most famous conquerors for free, in Firaxis' latest bid to coax you back to its controversial sequel
partialText: Tests of Time has one last surprise in store.

title: This indie action RPG looks like Minecraft but plays like Dark Messiah, letting you boot enemies off ledges and body slam them into walls of spikes
partialText: The Adventures of Sir Kicksalot is out now

title: Forza Horizon 6 has hit a higher peak player count than Forza Horizon 5 and it's not even out yet
partialText: Meching money.

title: It's time for Garfield's official Magic: The Gathering crossover now
partialText: No, not Richard Garfield. The other one.

title: Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has no interest in writing Half-Life 3: 'I don't want to touch that with a 10-foot pole'
partialText: "Or even a grav gun separating me from that 10-foot pole."

title: Lego racing game 2K Drive will be delisted next week, but online multiplayer won't shut down until next year
partialText: It released just three years ago.

title: Claims that Mixtape will be delisted over music licenses are 'a lie,' says publisher
partialText: The developer paid for perpetual music licenses to avoid that problem.

title: Ancient MMO Final Fantasy 11 still has new things on the horizon 24 years after launch
partialText: The other Final Fantasy MMO is still doing its thing.

title: Check your inbox: Steam Controller reservations are coming through
partialText: Not everyone got an email, but if you did, you'll have to act fast.

title: GTA roleplayers built a secret Boiler Room rave beneath Los Santos, complete with DJs, club photographers, biker security, and a custom party drug
partialText: With nearly 100 players packed into an underground bunker.

title: MMOs are better if classes are imbalanced—you just need to do it on purpose
partialText: Perfectly balanced, as all things shouldn't be.

title: This game about being a chaotic mage might be the best indie immersive sim you can play, as I learned after destroying a mime's house with magnetism
partialText: Rhell: Warped Worlds & Troubled Times is a delight.

title: I've been pixelating things again for our latest quiz—this time you have to guess which 10 videogame characters I've mangled
partialText: It's like going back to the 1980s.

title: MercurySteam announces 'difficult and painful' job cuts as its God of War-inspired hack 'n' slash arrives on Steam
partialText: The developer of Blades of Fire has initiated a "workforce adjustment process."

title: 6 million more people are using Firefox because of new EU rules, which is good news for Chrome haters like me
partialText: Other third-party browsers are seeing upticks too.

title: Sink your teeth into V Rising for free this weekend, and you can grab the full game for less than half price
partialText: All DLC is also 20% off.

title: Fallout's creator reveals you could have played as a snoring cow hater who believes in UFOs, had Black Isle stuck with its original licensed roleplaying system
partialText: Tim Cain spills the tea on "GURPS Fallout".

title: I’m waiting days between attempts to catch one fish in Final Fantasy 14 before it disappears for months, so don’t let anyone tell you raids are the ‘hardcore’ challenge
partialText: If you thought I was bad at dodging bright lines on the floor, wait until you've seen me fish.

title: A domain related to J-Pop idol phenomenon Love Live! went up for auction and the lead bid is a very sane $615 million
partialText: Love Live… Profit?!?

title: The Fortnite-Overwatch crossover means we're talking about Tracer's butt again
partialText: Because of course we are.

title: Videogame pirates tell other pirates to shut up about it after Subnautica 2 developers are taunted with illicit copies
partialText: A breach of pirate etiquette has even pirates siding with a Subnautica 2 designer.

title: Overwatch's lackluster 10th anniversary event will have its rewards improved next week, with more free stuff planned for later this year
partialText: Game director Aaron Keller acknowledged players' disappointment with the event on X.

title: Subnautica 2's early access roadmap promises quality-of-life additions, co-op improvements, and—eventually—new biomes and creatures
partialText: The ocean's got room for more.

title: We can thank a Jim Henson Company puppeteer for some of Valve's best animation work
partialText: TF2, Left 4 Dead, and Portal have some Fraggle Rock in them.

title: GamesRadar has decamped to Kyoto to bring you some killer world premieres and trailers straight out of BitSummit Punch 2026
partialText: We just came in and found a letter in Japanese on their desks. We assume this is what it says.

title: I'm tired of everything getting turned into a roguelite, but I'll make an exception for pinball
partialText: My weakness has been laser targeted.

title: Another metaverse is set to die in June
partialText: Holoearth, which just launched in 2024, is the latest proof that PC Gamer's Wes Fenlon was right.

title: Diablo 4 players become unkillable gods as a minor bug fix in Lord of Hatred turns into a major problem for Blizzard
partialText: A second bug with defensive items has given several classes the ability to become effectively immortal.

title: Valve's massive update to the Steam marketplace must be working, because a gun I had listed on there for years just sold for a cool 40 bucks
partialText: The only thing better than an item listing is a bigger item listing with more graphs.

title: The world of videogames is 'currently not well understood' with major decisions based on 'a limited, partial view', say industry organisations UKIE and OKRE
partialText: They've launched a new report calling for a more comprehensive and unified research framework.

title: Notorious videogame movie auteur Uwe Boll is returning to the director's chair with a spiritual successor to House of the Dead
partialText: Boll heard Paul W.S. Anderson is doing an official House of the Dead reboot for Sega, and he's not having it.

title: Baldur's Gate 2 almost had a 'time travel plot', letting you visit an alternate future where BG1's main villain rules the Sword Coast
partialText: Sadly Sarevok never got his do-over.

title: Framework says its Wireless Touchpad Keyboard 'is by far our most waitlisted product'
partialText: Might be a bit galling for a company that's better known for making laptops.

title: We're getting closer to a 100% ROG rig as Asus gets into the DRAM game for its 20th anniversary
partialText: It might just be a one-off, though.

title: Forza Horizon 6's return to 'wristband progression' isn't the stand-in for a career mode I wanted it to be, but maybe that's for the best
partialText: Be car-ful what you wish for.

title: Rig R5 Spear Max HD gaming headset review
partialText: A very interesting wired headset, with some tuning I can't quite get my head around.

title: After close to 140 hours with it, I think Slay the Spire 2 feels more like a sequel than a DLC, even if Megacrit was forced to make it
partialText: Not just a shuffle of the deck.

title: I was worried EverQuest Legends making me too OP would ruin the magic of the classic MMO, but crushing hordes of frogloks is incredibly satisfying
partialText: Friction is great, but triple-classing isn't so bad, either.

title: Despite Donald Trump and Jensen Huang flying out to the country, China has not yet approved the sale of Nvidia AI chips
partialText: This is after Trump turned up in China to increase AI trade.

title: I really hope you weren't considering a GPU upgrade this year, as Nvidia may raise the price of the already pricey RTX 5090 by as much as $300
partialText: Memory is proving an expensive problem.

title: 'I just need to disappear, go into a cabin': Eric Barone has found the answer to Haunted Chocolatier's development distractions
partialText: Barone has dedicated five days a week to Haunted Chocolatier.

title: Hot on the heels of Apple's iPhone-in-a-laptop, Google and Intel have teamed up to give us the Googlebook
partialText: No word on the hardware yet, but Panther or Wildcat Lake are the most likely options.

title: How to get the Repair Tool in Subnautica 2
partialText: Repair your vehicles, bases, and facilities with one click.

title: Sketch group Aunty Donna's new parody of Black Mirror's Bandersnatch episode will send you on a 40-minute unskippable walk around Melbourne if you make the wrong choices
partialText: Bandersketch invites you to help the boys make their next video... as long as you can make the right choices.

title: An engineer has worked out how to speed up a 3D printer by 1000% with a Nintendo Switch, though 'for most people, a Raspberry Pi is a better choice'
partialText: That's one way to fight e-waste.

title: Intel's 270K Plus is worthy of being picked by Thermal Grizzly as a delidded option, and it's even cheaper than a stock 285K
partialText: One for the serious clockers only but I still kinda want one.
